{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Parse revenue: remove commas and convert to float
df['revenue'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Remove QA orders (revenue == 999999.99)
df = df[df['revenue'] != 999999.99]

# Now, compute conversion rate by customer_segment on the full dataset (all rows, including refunded)
# Conversion rate = number of converted orders / total orders in segment
# Note: 'converted' is 1 only if checkout completed. Refunded orders are still counted as 'converted' if they were completed first.
# But: the data dictionary says 'converted' is 1 if the order completed checkout — so even if refunded, it was converted.
# So we keep all rows.
# Compute group stats
df_grouped = df.groupby('customer_segment', as_index=False)['converted'].agg(['count', 'sum'])
df_grouped.columns = ['segment', 'total_orders', 'converted_orders']
df_grouped['conversion_rate'] = df_grouped['converted_orders'] / df_grouped['total_orders']

# Sort by conversion rate descending
df_grouped_sorted = df_grouped.sort_values('conversion_rate', ascending=False)

# Get the segment with highest conversion rate
highest_segment = df_grouped_sorted.iloc[0]['segment']

# Print the full result
df_grouped_sorted, highest_segment"}
